newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's state works bank Banobras places bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's state works bank Banobras places bond.

text.p: Mexico's state works bank Banco Nacional de Obras y Servicios Publicos, known as Banobras, said Monday it had placed $200 million in bonds on international markets.
The issue, with a seven-year maturity, will pay a coupon of 9.625 percent and is registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the bank said.
Banobras said the issue lengthens its existing debt, reduces financing costs and diversifies its debt base.
The bonds were placed among 100 institutional investors of the United States, Europe and Asia.
Banobras said orders were received totaling $400 million.
It gave no reason why it did not place more bonds, given the demand.
Lead agents were Morgan Stanley, Lehman Brothers and J.P. Morgan, the bank said.
